title: How to pay with your Android phone anywhere in the world
summary: It's easier than you think to pay with your phone while traveling.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority Google likes to make its products needlessly convoluted, and nowhere is this more evident than with Google Pay and Google Wallet. While one service would’ve done the job — like Apple Pay and Samsung Pay — Google has a confusing system that necessitates an article (such as this one) to decode. Basically, Google Wallet is what you use to store payment cards, make in-store and online payments in the U.S. and other western countries. Google Pay itself isn’t available as a standalone app other than in India and Singapore, with Google shutting down the app in most global markets in 2022 and in the U.S. after 2024. Why did Google do this, you ask? Because it saw that Wallet was being used five times as much, so it folded in most features of Google Pay into Wallet. Now, Google Pay basically works as a transaction layer within Wallet.
